findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the raw-only noise-floor metrics against the existing e6_metrics.py/e6_judge_reliability.py prior art — either reuse e6_metrics (raw_agreement/fleiss_kappa/jaccard) or state explicitly why organic identical-material pairs warrant a raw-only, un-chance-corrected metric.
evidence: Plan publishes only raw-agreement figures: '(a) verdict flip rate; (b) per-criterion finding churn (Jaccard by norm_id); (c) per-question Pass-2 agreement ... agreement is micro-averaged: (# ... old==new) / (total ...)'.

Existing prior art: docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/e6_metrics.py:178 compute_agreement returns BOTH 'fleiss_kappa' and 'raw_agreement' with documented KAPPA_FLOOR/RAW_FLOOR and category_counts; e6_judge_reliability.py:9 'measures agreement (Fleiss' κ + raw)'.
e6_metrics.py:203 already provides a `jaccard(a, b)` helper — the plan re-specifies 'Jaccard by norm_id' without referencing it.

The plan's 'noise floor' answers the same underlying question as E6 (how consistent is the plan-review judge on materially-identical input); raw agreement without a chance-corrected companion (κ) is exactly the pitfall E6 already addresses, and is more acute here because organic identical-material pairs can have a skewed verdict base rate.
findings.finding: The reviewer-noise-floor measurement reinvents an internal judge-reliability methodology (e6_metrics.py / e6_judge_reliability.py) without citing or reconciling with it, and publishes only raw agreement where the established approach pairs raw agreement with chance-corrected Fleiss' kappa.
findings.location: Approach → 'Noise floor' bullet; AC 'The noise floor ... per-question agreement with its pooled comparison count'
scenarios: A published verdict-flip / per-question raw-agreement figure looks reassuringly high purely because most pairs share a dominant verdict/answer, when a chance-corrected κ would reveal near-chance agreement.
A later ticket that consumes the noise floor as a calibration threshold silently diverges from the E6 floors already committed in the repo.
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Noise floor' bullet, reference docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/e6_metrics.py and either (a) reuse its jaccard/raw_agreement/fleiss_kappa helpers so the floor is chance-corrected and comparable to the committed E6 figures, or (b) add a one-line rationale for why per-question/per-pair raw agreement is reported without κ (e.g. verdict base-rate is published alongside so readers can chance-correct themselves).
